name: Work that happens in the background
summary: Jobs that run after the page has already responded, and retry themselves when they fail.

provenance.source: SimpleHire — its queue and worker design, in particular the retry-with-backoff and dead-letter behaviour
provenance.changes: Redis and BullMQ replaced with the PostgreSQL the project already has, using SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. One fewer service to run, pay for and monitor, at the cost of throughput a small app will not reach.

extensionPoints.description: Your jobs. Add one function per kind of work.

postInstall: The worker has to be running for jobs to happen. Shipyard starts it alongside your app.
limitations: Built on your database rather than a dedicated queue. Fine into the thousands of jobs an hour; not a replacement for a real queue at high volume.
Jobs run at least once, not exactly once. A job that charges a card must check whether it already did.
